steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Recursive Sparse Attention: Million-Token Length Extrapolation at Logarithmic Cost
summary: Replaces dense attention over the full KV cache with a hierarchical tree that summarizes the cache using distilled pooling keys, selecting tokens at logarithmic cost. Requires training a pooler per layer on 0.62B tokens and deploying custom optimized kernels; adds complexity to the inference stack and requires distillation from the target model. Failures can occur if the pooler misses relevant long-range dependencies or if custom kernels contain implementation bugs that affect production stability.
rationale: Adoption requires custom optimized kernels and distillation training from the specific foundation model, which exceeds current infrastructure and depends on unavailable implementation details.

claims.statement: Replaces dense attention over the full KV cache with a hierarchical tree that summarizes the cache using distilled pooling keys, selecting tokens at logarithmic cost. Requires training a pooler per layer on 0.62B tokens and deploying custom optimized kernels; adds complexity to the inference stack and requires distillation from the target model. Failures can occur if the pooler misses relevant long-range dependencies or if custom kernels contain implementation bugs that affect production stability.
RecSA accelerates prefill by 3.2x and decoding by 3.8x compared with dense attention at 524K tokens on one H200 GPU.
